questions.q: What did Edward Lorenz notice while modeling the weather?
a: Tiny rounding changes drastically altered the forecast
Weather could be predicted months in advance
Small inputs never affect large systems
Butterflies avoid regions with storms
questions.why: Lesson 1 says dropping even a third decimal point made his whole weather study turn out completely differently.

questions.q: What does the butterfly effect describe?
a: A tiny change can dramatically alter a whole system
Order always emerges from apparent disorder
Chaos disappears once enough data is gathered
Large causes always produce large effects
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the butterfly in Beijing and the storm in New York to show how small acts reshape outcomes.

questions.q: According to the summary, what is chaos?
a: A basic feature of how the universe works
A mathematical error in early models
A problem better computers will solve
A theory modern science has rejected
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues chaos is a law of nature, as real as the predictable laws we usually study.

questions.q: What happened when scientists added factors like limited food to population models?
a: The populations behaved completely differently
The models became perfectly predictable
The populations grew without any limit
The extra factors changed nothing
questions.why: Lesson 2 says adding even one overlooked factor produced chaos instead of the expected pattern.

questions.q: What did the Dynamic System Collective do?
a: Used computers to alter starting conditions and watch results
Built the first satellites for weather forecasting
Set out to prove chaos theory was false
Founded the modern field of economics
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes the group changing small factors at the start of a system and observing how its course shifted.
